newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran conservatives back speaker for president.
newsitem.headline: Iran conservatives back speaker for president.

text.p: Two leading Iranian conservative clergy groups have picked parliamentary speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri as their candidate in next year's presidential election, Tehran newspapers said on Monday.

The daily Iran News said an influential group of Shi'ite Moslem theologians in the holy city of Qom nominated Nateq-Nouri for the elections which will decide the successor of President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani.

Akhbar daily quoted parliamentarians as saying the Combatant Clergy Association (CCA), Iran's main conservative group, also nominated Nateq-Nouri for the summer 1997 race but would not announce it officially until Thursday.
Rafsanjani, who is serving his second term, is barred by the constitution from running for a third consecutive term.
Akhbar said former prime minister Mir Hossein Mousavi, widely promoted by centrists and radical groups as a strong candidate to pit against Nateq-Nouri, announced his "definite refusal" to run.

With Mousavi out of the race, Nateq-Nouri remained the most prominant potential candidate for the presidency, Iran's top executive position after a 1989 constitutional reform removed the post of prime minister.
Nateq-Nouri, a Shi'ite cleric, is the leader of the majority conservatives in parliament who defend the stricter adherence to religious and social norms of the 1979 Islamic revolution.

They have slowed Rafsanjani's economic liberalisation plans to prevent losing popular support among the poor after the reforms lead to a widespread outcry over rapid price rises and increased unemployment.

But the conservatives, traditionally close to bazaar merchants, have opposed any return to a state-run economy set up during the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq war and instead advocated more gradual market reforms.
Nateq-Nouri has in the past year kept a high profile in the media prompting widespread expectations that he would run, but he has not officially announced his candidacy.
